context: Fix each defect independently and prove it with a test, not a convention. Give each project a distinct distribution or import name (or add a root pytest config that maps the four suites), make pilot scoring read the predeclared pilot set and refuse to overwrite a report whose run set differs, parameterize the generation constants so any committed generation can be re-audited by flag, and narrow the transcript tripwire to sessions the runner itself could have created (nonce, model pin, or session id correlation) rather than any new file.
description: Four defects confirmed by direct reproduction on 2026-07-29 against main at f801885. One, four projects (memory_tooling, memory_tooling/claude, memory_tooling/codex, evaluation_runs/behavioral) all expose the same top-level package name memory_tooling, so a repo-root pytest fails with 7 collection errors and each suite only runs under its own --project root; a reviewer running the obvious command sees red on green code. Two, the v5 item rung 3 re-runs score --pilot --enforce-pilot-thresholds, which after the full fill rescores 180 runs into the committed 45-run pilot report, overwrites it, and prints false blockers; recovery needed git checkout. Three, audit.py and score.py hardcode results-vN, isolation-vN, preflight-vN, and the schema_version check, so v3 and v4 evidence cannot be re-audited or re-scored without a historical checkout, weakening the immutability claim the packets rely on. Four, the runner treats ANY new file matching ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl as an isolation failure, so an unrelated concurrent human session fails the run; this fired on the v3 144-run matrix and needed manual re-attestation.

work_units.evidence: commit b406bdf. Two independent fixes: --pilot now selects the predeclared codex pilot subset so the gate reproduces its verdict after the fill instead of rescoring all 180; and _refuse_clobber rejects writing a report over one covering a different run set (clear message, exit 2, --force override). Proven end to end: the exact invocation that destroyed the committed pilot report now exits 2 with 'summarizes 45 run(s) and this invocation covers 0' and diff confirms the committed report is byte-unchanged. 4 regression tests added (-k 'pilot or clobber' = 6 passed)
work_units.summary: Make pilot scoring read the predeclared pilot set and fail closed instead of overwriting a committed report with a different run set

work_units.evidence: commit 5fbf5e6. audit.py exposes results_dir(generation)/isolation_name(generation)/DEFAULT_GENERATION and both audit and score take --generation. Proven: audit --generation v3|v4|v5 each runs from current main against the right evidence set (v3 output names claude-* runs that exist only in v3). Scoring an older generation correctly refuses because prompts/oracles/response schema are generation-specific, now as a clean message + exit 2 instead of a traceback. Rung 3 (audit --generation v3) passes - it reports the genuine evidence loss rather than a tooling failure. 2 tests added
work_units.summary: Parameterize the generation constants so v3, v4, and v5 evidence can each be re-audited and re-scored from current main

work_units.evidence: commit 2f04f0a. _transcript_is_evaluation_owned attributes a new transcript by the two properties an eval session pins - cwd = governance repo AND model = claude-opus-4-6 - so the real 2026-07-29 false positive (session 84cff73e, cwd BenchBox, model claude-opus-5) no longer fails a run. Manifest now separates new_session_transcripts from leaked_session_transcripts and only the latter drives unchanged/exit. Fails safe: matching both still fails, and an unreadable transcript is treated as a leak. 4 tests, all matched by the rung's -k transcript selector
work_units.summary: Narrow the transcript tripwire to evaluation-owned sessions so an unrelated concurrent session cannot fail an otherwise isolated run
